question: Hydrophobic side chains gathering inside and hydrophilic ones facing the water outside is what drives a chain into its _____, the shape it actually works in.
questions: Individually the bonds holding it are thirty to three hundred times weaker than a covalent one, so _____ is stable only because so many of them act together.
Deep-learning methods can now generate sequences meant to fold into a chosen _____, including shapes that no organism has ever used.
abstract:
The tertiary structure of a protein is the folding of one polypeptide chain into its three-dimensional shape, produced by interactions between side chains that lie in quite different regions of the sequence. The decisive one is the sorting of hydrophobic side chains into the interior and hydrophilic ones onto the surface, where they meet water. Helices and sheets can sit in that hydrophobic core because backbone hydrogen bonding has already neutralised the polar character of their CO and NH groups, while the loops joining them lie on the outside. Hydrogen bonds and ionic bonds between polar side chains at the surface matter as well, and covalent disulfide bonds between cysteines stabilise many secreted and cell-surface proteins. Taken singly the non-covalent bonds are thirty to three hundred times weaker than a covalent bond, so a fold holds only because a great many of them act in parallel.

Helices and sheets joined by loops fold into compact globular units called domains, the basic units of tertiary structure; a small protein such as myoglobin has one, and a large protein several, often with distinct functions. Because a domain is a unit it can be reused, and gene duplication has produced families whose members share sequence and fold alike, among them the serine proteases: chymotrypsin, trypsin, elastase and several enzymes of blood clotting. Comparing genomes shows the same process at scale, and a survey of 446 plant genomes found land plants carrying more domains and more domain combinations than algae, with shuffling generating the new combinations. A fold is not fixed once made, and non-reducing proteomics finds oxidative stress remodelling disulfide bonding across more than a thousand proteins. Folds no organism has used can now be designed as well, since deep learning has shifted protein design from optimising energy functions to generating sequence and structure together.
